title: Friday night journal
description: Demo conversation (synthetic, for the demo account). Alex records a late-night voice journal about the week, moving from the job decision to that morning's run, a Stoic idea from coffee with Priya, and missing family, before coming back to the job decision.

utterances.text: Okay. Friday, it's almost midnight. I said I'd do these more often, so here I am, talking to my phone in the dark like a normal person.

Big thing this week is obviously the studio offer. I countered on Wednesday, like Dana said. Excited, specific number, then shut up. The silence was horrible. Maybe four seconds, and it felt like a minute.
They said they'd get back to me Monday. So now I just wait. Which I'm bad at.

Anyway. Different thing. The run this morning was actually good? Jordan sent the plan, like they said they would, and today was supposed to be an easy six k. And I kept it easy. Like actually slow. And my knee didn't do the sharp thing at all.
I did the step-downs and the glute bridges after, which, wow, my legs were shaking on the step-downs. Very humbling. But it's the first time in weeks running hasn't felt like a fight.
Rest day tomorrow. Jordan's voice in my head saying rest days are training.
The other thing I keep coming back to is the coffee with Priya on Tuesday. The Stoic thing. What's up to me and what isn't.
Because I realized this week I spend most of my energy on the second list. The claims team, my manager, whether the studio says yes on Monday. None of that is mine.
What's mine is, did I do good work today. Did I say the hard thing early. Did I treat people okay. And honestly, on those, this week was fine. Better than fine.
There's a Seneca line I looked up after, something like, we suffer more in imagination than in reality. Which is basically my whole four a.m. routine.
I miss my family. That's sort of out of nowhere, but it's true. Mom called on Wednesday and I was in the middle of something and I said I'd call back and I didn't.
It's her birthday in two weeks. I should actually go home for it instead of just sending flowers. Flights are not that expensive if I book soon.
I think part of it is talking to Sam about church, and Sam saying they'd been lonely. I didn't realize how much I'd stopped calling people. Even my brother. We used to text every day.
Okay. Call Mom tomorrow. Actually call, not text.
So, back to the job. If I'm honest with myself, I think I've already decided. If they meet me even halfway on the money, I'm going to take it.
It's scary. I've never designed anything you can walk around. But Dana's right, feeling out of my depth is probably the point.
And if they say no on Monday, then that's on the not-up-to-me list. I'll still know I want to do work I'm proud of. That's the part I keep.
Okay. That's it. Go to sleep, Alex.
